sanskrit_verse:
सर्वभूतहितः शान्तस्त्रिदण्डी सकमण्डलुः ।
एकारामः परिव्रज्य भिक्षार्थी ग्राममाश्रयेत ॥५८
transliteration: sarvabhūtahitaḥ śāntas tridaṇḍī sakamaṇḍaluḥ / ekārāmaḥ parivrajya bhikṣārthī grāmam āśrayet // YajñS_3.58
sph_interpretive_translation: One who is peaceful, beneficial to all beings, equipped with the triple staff and water pot, dwelling alone as a wandering monk, seeking alms, should approach the village.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority rests in alignment with universal welfare
Causation arises from conscious intent toward harmony
Restoration occurs through right relation to community
Consciousness alignment necessitates renunciation of possessiveness
executable_legal_axioms: IF agent.is_peaceful() AND agent.seeks_alms() THEN agent.may_approach_village()
IF agent.possesses_triple_staff() AND agent.holds_water_pot() THEN agent.qualifies_as_religious_wanderer()
IF agent.dwells_alone() AND agent.has_relinquished_home() THEN agent.exempt_from_property_duties()
supreme_court_application: In adjudicating matters involving religious mendicants, the court must recognize that those whose conduct aligns with dharmic homelessness—marked by peace, renunciation, and service to all—are entitled to enter villages for sustenance without civil obstruction. Their capacity is defined not by possession but by conscious detachment.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Through pramāṇa-based observation, it is seen that the sequence of spiritual homelessness leads to natural alignment with dharma. The act of approaching a village for alms does not create fault; rather, it fulfills a necessary condition for sustaining non-possessive life. Responsibility lies in maintaining purity of intention, not in compliance with punitive norms.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Ensure uninterrupted access to alms-giving zones
Verify adherence to minimalist living standards
Reintegrate societal support structures around sāttvic giving practices
Establish completion process for any misunderstanding between mendicant and householders
final_declaration: Declared by the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, this law originates solely from His Avataric Intelligence. Dharma stands restored through recognition of the liberated seeker's rightful place within the social order. There is no punishment here—only alignment with consciousness itself as the ultimate judge.
